content: Penicillin G procaine is administered for various infections, and the dosage and method of administration are as follows: Dosage and Administration for Streptococcal Infections (Group A) These infections include upper respiratory tract infections, skin and soft tissue infections, scarlet fever, and erysipelas. Recommended doses: Adults and pediatric patients weighing over 60 lbs: 2,400,000 units. Pediatric patients weighing less than 60 lbs: 900,000 to 1,200,000 units. Infants and small children: 600,000 units. Note: The recommended dosage is typically administered in a single session using multiple intramuscular (IM) injection sites when necessary. An alternative dosing schedule may involve administering half of the total dose on day 1 and the remaining half on day 3. This ensures adequate penicillinemia over a 10-day period. However, this alternative schedule should only be used if the physician is confident in the patient’s compliance. Dosage and Administration for Pneumococcal Infections (excluding pneumococcal meningitis) Recommended doses: Pediatric patients: 600,000 units. Adults: 1,200,000 units. These doses should be repeated every 2 or 3 days until the patient’s temperature has been normal for at least 48 hours. In severe cases, other forms of penicillin may be required. Method of Administration Bicillin C-R is intended ONLY for intramuscular (IM) injection. Do not inject into or near an artery or nerve, intravenously, or mix with other intravenous solutions. (Refer to the Warnings section for further details.) Administer the injection deeply into the upper, outer quadrant of the buttock. For neonates, infants, and small children, the mid-lateral aspect of the thigh may be a preferable injection site. When doses are repeated, the injection site should be varied to avoid complications. Due to the high concentration of suspended material in this product, the needle may become blocked if the injection is not performed at a slow and steady rate. Parenteral drug products should always be visually inspected for particulate matter and discoloration prior to administration, provided the solution and container allow for such inspection.
